Package com.nexuslink.ui.files

package com.nexuslink.ui.files
  • Class
    Description
    BulkRename
    Computes the new names for a multi-file rename, the way a commander's "batch rename" dialog does: an optional find/replace (literal or regex), prefix/suffix, sequential numbering via a {n} token, and a case transform — all applied to the base name while the extension is preserved.
    BulkRename.Case
    How to recase the resulting base name.
    BulkRename.Result
    One before → after row.
    BulkRename.Rule
    The transform to apply.
    Checksum
    SHA-256 digests of file content, used by TransferQueue to prove a transferred file arrived byte-for-byte rather than merely at the right length (TransferIntegrity compares the two digests).
    DirectoryDiff
    A single-level comparison of two directory listings — the "left" (e.g.
    DirectoryDiff.Digests
    Supplies a file's content digest, or null when none is available.
    DirectoryDiff.Entry
    One reconciled row.
    DirectoryDiff.Match
    How two same-named files are told apart.
    DirectoryDiff.Status
    How a matched name relates across the two listings.
    DiskSpace
    Free/total capacity of the volume backing a directory, for the commander's per-pane status line.
    DualPaneBrowser
    The WinSCP/MobaXterm-style two-pane file commander: the local disk on the left, a remote service on the right, with Upload → / ← Download controls in between.
    DuplicateName
    Computes a non-colliding name for a "Duplicate" of a file, the way a commander does it: the first duplicate of report.txt is report copy.txt, then report copy 2.txt, report copy 3.txt, … Duplicating something that is already a copy increments the counter (report copy.txt → report copy 2.txt) rather than stacking suffixes.
    FileBrowserPane
    One pane of the DualPaneBrowser: an address bar, a navigation toolbar (Up / Refresh / New Folder) and a details table (name · size · modified · permissions) over a FileSystem.
    FileBrowserPane.CrossPaneDrop
    A drop of items from the other pane: the items, the destination directory, and whether it is a move.
    FileDetails
    Builds the label/value rows shown in a file's Properties dialog from a FileItem, plus the pure symbolic→octal permission conversion behind them.
    FileDetails.Row
    One label/value row in the properties view.
    FileFilter
    The in-pane view filter for a FileBrowserPane: an optional "show hidden" (dotfile) toggle plus a case-insensitive quick-filter substring over the entry name.
    FileItem
    One entry in a FileSystem listing — local or remote.
    FileOrder
    The default ordering for a FileBrowserPane listing, matching what file commanders like WinSCP / Norton Commander show: the synthetic ".." row first, then directories before files, and within each group a case-insensitive name sort.
    FileOrder.SortKey
    The column a user can sort a listing by (matches the FileBrowserPane table columns).
    FileSystem
    A navigable file system backing one pane of the DualPaneBrowser — either the local disk (LocalFileSystem) or a remote service (SFTP/FTP).
    FileTransfer
    Moves bytes between the local disk and a remote service (SFTP/FTP) for the two-pane browser.
    LocalFileSystem
    The local disk as a FileSystem, so the same browser pane can show local files next to a remote SFTP/FTP listing (the WinSCP/MobaXterm two-pane layout).
    NavHistory
    Pure, JavaFX-free back/forward navigation history for a single FileBrowserPane — a browser-style visited-path stack with a movable cursor.
    ObjectPath
    Pure, dependency-free path math for the object-storage commander.
    OverwriteResolver
    Decides, for each target file that already exists, whether the transfer should overwrite it or skip it — honouring "…all" answers for the remainder of the batch.
    OverwriteResolver.Action
    The resolved per-file action.
    OverwriteResolver.Choice
    The answers a user can give when a target file already exists.
    PathBookmarks
    An ordered, path-unique list of directory bookmarks for a file pane ("favourite" folders the user can jump back to).
    PathBookmarks.Bookmark
    One saved location: a display label for a directory path.
    PathCrumbs
    Splits a file-system path into clickable breadcrumb segments — root → … → current — by walking up via the owning FileSystem's parent function, so it works for both POSIX-style remote paths ("/home/user") and local OS paths.
    PathCrumbs.Crumb
    One breadcrumb: the label shown to the user and the full path it navigates to.
    QuickView
    Pure, JavaFX-free classifier deciding how the commander should quick-view a file: as editable text, a read-only image preview, or not at all.
    QuickView.Kind
    How a file may be opened in the quick-view dialog.
    QuickViewDialog
    The quick-view / edit-in-place dialog: reads a file's bytes off the FX thread (up to a size cap) and shows them as either an editable text area or a read-only image preview, per QuickView.
    ResumePlan
    Decides whether an interrupted transfer can pick up where it left off, given the source's size and the size of whatever partial file is sitting at the destination.
    ResumePlan.Action
    What to do with a destination file that already holds some bytes.
    ResumePlan.Plan
    A verdict plus the byte offset to start from (0 unless the action is ResumePlan.Action.RESUME_FROM).
    RetryPolicy
    Auto-retry rule for transfers that fail with a transient error: how many attempts to make in total and how long to back off between them (exponential, capped).
    SameSideMove
    Plans a same-side move — dragging entries into a folder on the very same FileSystem — as a set of FileSystem.rename(java.lang.String, java.lang.String) operations rather than a copy-and-delete.
    SameSideMove.Move
    One planned rename: item moves from from to to.
    SavedSessions
    An ordered, name-unique list of saved connection profiles ("sessions") for a file-style connector, plus the last local/remote directory each one was left in — the WinSCP/MobaXterm "quick connect to a server and land where I was" behaviour.
    SavedSessions.Session
    One saved profile.
    SessionMenu
    The connect bar's Sessions drop-down: save the filled-in connection form as a named profile, quick-connect to a saved one, or forget it.
    SyncBrowsing
    Pure path math for the commander's "synchronized browsing" mode: when one pane navigates, the other should make the same relative move (descend into the same sub-folders, or climb the same number of levels).
    SyncPlanner
    Turns a DirectoryDiff into an ordered list of concrete SyncPlanner.Actions to reconcile two panes — the planning core of SyncService (7.1).
    SyncPlanner.Action
    One planned operation.
    SyncPlanner.Mode
    The reconciliation strategy chosen by the user.
    SyncPlanner.Op
    The primitive a planned SyncPlanner.Action performs.
    TransferErrors
    Classifies a transfer failure as transient (worth an automatic retry — a dropped connection, a timeout, a temporarily unreachable host) or permanent (bad credentials, missing file, no permission — retrying won't help).
    TransferGovernor
    Pause/resume + bandwidth-throttle control for the TransferQueue, applied at the one place every FileTransfer implementation already reports through: the cumulative-bytes progress callback (called per 64 KB chunk).
    TransferGovernor.Sleeper
    Sleeps for the given number of milliseconds; injectable so tests can record instead of wait.
    TransferIntegrity
    Verifies a completed transfer by comparing the source against what actually landed on the destination: the byte count must match, and — when the caller can supply a checksum for both sides — the digests must match too.
    TransferIntegrity.Issue
    A specific way a transfer failed verification.
    TransferIntegrity.Report
    The verdict for one file.
    TransferItem
    One queued file transfer in a TransferQueue.
    TransferItem.Direction
    Transfer direction relative to the two-pane browser (local ⇄ remote).
    TransferQueue
    Drives the existing FileTransfer copy logic for a batch of TransferItems, exposing observable per-item and overall progress.
    TransferQueue.Listener
    Receives queue change notifications (off any thread — UI listeners must marshal to FX).
    TransferQueuePanel
    A collapsible panel showing the live TransferQueue: a table with per-row progress bars, an overall progress bar, status counts and a "Clear completed" button.
    TransferStatus
    Lifecycle of a single TransferItem as it moves through the TransferQueue.

NexusLink — one console, every protocol, zero context switching.
